outline.chapter_title: 1. Introduction to Diffusion Models and the Need for Fine‑Tuning
outline.description: Sets the scientific context by reviewing recent progress in text‑to‑image diffusion, explains the challenge of providing fine‑controlled generation, and introduces the two target downstream tasks – subject‑driven generation and controllable generation. It also motivates why preserving pre‑training performance during fine‑tuning is essential.
subtopics: Overview of large text‑to‑image diffusion models (Stable Diffusion, Imagen, etc.)
Limitations of pure text guidance – ambiguity and lack of precision
Definition of subject‑driven generation (DreamBooth style)
Definition of controllable generation (ControlNet, T2I‑Adapter style)
Key desiderata for a fine‑tuning method: efficiency, generalizability preservation
Shortcomings of existing fine‑tuning strategies (small LR updates, LoRA low‑rank adapters)

outline.description: Introduces the core concept of OFT – learning a layer‑shared orthogonal transformation that preserves pairwise neuron angles and therefore the hyperspherical energy of the network. Explains how this property can maintain semantic structure while allowing controlled adaptation.
subtopics: Why neuron direction matters – angular information as semantic carrier (toy CAE experiment)
Orthogonal transformations preserve pairwise angles – hyperspherical energy invariance
Derivation of OFT constraint ≠RᵀR=I and W=RW⁰
Proof that minimal hyperspherical energy difference yields W=RW⁰
Comparison with LoRA: multiplicative vs additive weight updates

outline.description: Describes practical techniques to implement OFT on large networks without prohibitive parameter cost. Covers Cayley parametrization and block‑diagonal decomposition, and analyzes parameter complexity relative to LoRA.
subtopics: Cayley transform R=(I+Q)(I−Q)⁻¹ for generating orthogonal matrices
Skew‑symmetric matrix Q and its constraints
Block‑diagonal orthogonal matrices to reduce parameters (r blocks)
Parameter count analysis for R vs LoRA low‑rank updates
Sharing blocks across layers as an additional reduction

outline.description: Extends OFT by adding an explicit radius constraint on the orthogonal transform to further limit deviation from the pre‑trained weights, improving stability and convergence.
subtopics: COFT forward pass with ≠RᵀR=I and ||R−I||≤ϵ
Mapping radius constraint onto skew matrix Q via Neumann series expansion
Projected gradient descent on Q to enforce ||Q||≤ϵ′
Practical choice of ϵ for different tasks
Empirical impact of ϵ on stability vs flexibility

outline.description: Presents a lightweight extension that allows per‑neuron scaling while still preserving hyperspherical energy, thereby increasing expressiveness with negligible extra parameters.
